eligibility: ClipVault is preparing its first public release. It is a Windows clipboard manager with encrypted DuckDB storage, safe rich-text previews, and token-scoped read-only HTTP/MCP access. There are no verified public stars, downloads, or external adoption metrics yet. Its potential value is a locally controlled, auditable bridge between clipboard history and developer tools; broad ecosystem impact is not yet demonstrated.
api_usage: I plan to use API credits for maintainer-reviewed pull request checks, issue triage, synthetic security regression cases, and release verification. Automation would inspect source code and sanitized fixtures, never real clipboard databases, passwords, API tokens, or signing keys. Humans would approve changes and publication. These API workflows are planned, not currently deployed.
additional: ClipVault uses Apache-2.0 for project-owned source and documentation, attributed to ClipVault contributors. Offline activation code remains included; recipients may modify and redistribute under the license. The release branch retains development history after excluding internal materials. Source is hosted on GitHub; Windows binary acceptance and distribution notices remain open. Support contacts are foobar placeholders. No OpenAI application has been submitted.
